title: To what extent can AI (Claude for example) optimize your game / improve FPS, etc.
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
They say it's the just as much the user as it is the tools. I am inclined to agree. With this latest AI leak, twitter comments were cracking up at how the guys getting it to run on PC were just like "Make it run better, make no mistakes". And they're actually making progress!

What's your formula for optimization? I managed to eek out 12-15 more frames which is terrific but it's just not enough and now I am spinning my wheels.

comments.author: Enderoth
comments.body:
Every time I've had a slow-down, stutter, load felt long, etc., Opus 5.5 has been able to eliminate it or greatly ameliorate it. I will prompt it to look online for best practices or advice/posts on the same kind of issue, suggest fixes myself from experience, or review things I just did that might be causing the slowdown.

I don't do anything too crazy--mostly low poly and 2d/2.5d stuff, but it's always managed to increase efficiency. It's often best to let it run polishing and performance testing suites on an otherwise quiet machine for good baseline.

comments.author: throwaway09234023322
comments.body: "Claude, people's lives depend on this game running at 60 fps. Don't fuck this up. Make no mistakes"

comments.author: prettyfuckingfarfrom
comments.body:
Tell it to give you a performance breakdown, and then try to think outside of the box on what you can cut/fake to get the same effect but for less cost

For example I had bots that walked around and loaded cannons on a ship, and the performance was terrible. Claude broke it down and told me that 60% of the cost was purely the bots thinking. So instead of having the bots load cannons, I had the cannons load and fire themselves, and replaced the thinking bots with “dummies” that can still be killed and do loading/firing animations. So same effect but went from 20fps to 60+

Find the bottleneck and get creative.

comments.author: OutOfTokensStudios
comments.body: Hook up performance telemetry in the game, it gives the llm superpowers to be able to narrow down issues. If you give it that plus the performance tools of your chosen engine you can do some amazing things

comments.author: Responsible-Ebb1722
comments.body: Those "make no mistakes" posts are jokes. Sure there might be a couple slop kiddies playing around, but the real progress is being made by engineers that have been hacking games for decades.

comments.author: WetPlug88
comments.body:
"Make it better, make no mistakes" will obviously do SOMETHING 
The point is that as an example "Optimise the CPU load with the water shader refraction and vertex displacement by moving the logic to the GPU save for all elements which must be read-back by CPU eg. vertex heights, where read-back would cost more than .2ms" is going to do it a lot better and a lot faster.

If you don't know what you're doing AI makes you a bit faster and a bit better.

If you know what you're doing AI makes you 100x faster.

comments.author: TLDReddit73
comments.body: Working on a survival game with Godot and Opus. I have a day/night cycle with shadows that move quite fast.  The movement causes the shadows in trees and from trees to flicker and move a lot.  I played with all kinds of settings and couldn’t get it much better.  I eventually had an idea to have the shadows be forecast and then morph from the present shadow to the future.  I asked Opus to do that and have a control so I could adjust to find the right speed.  It just did it and worked great in the game.  The tree shadows look like they just slightly sway with the wind.  I was amazed.  Bottom line is, think outside the box and ask for what seems like might be really hard.  It just might work.

comments.author: Dan_Fury
comments.body:
I have a second PC running with Claude in the same network. It regularly pulls the game and runs soak tests, then reports it's finding to the first PC which then optimizes over night. This has given a tremendous performance boost to my games and the AI is doing a better job finding performance holes and hidden leaks than any QA team that I have been a part of in the 26 years I have worked in the industry.
I wish I had a third PC to decimate and optimize all Models all the time to really get the maximum performance possible.

comments.author: Neither_Berry_100
comments.body: The question is how did it improve performance? Did it do something like reduce render distance which also changes the game experience? Did they optimize for pc hardware? The best pcs are more powerful than a ps5. So it might just be a hardware difference. Did it find and fix a dumb bug costing lots of performance? Or did it actually do a real improvement? Or did it fix a bug that was it's own fault in the first place?

comments.author: Mrbuttshaman
comments.body: Extremely good.  Ask claude to prepare a prompt for gemini deep research on optimization techniques for the specific type of game you are making.  Feed that research report back into Claude and ask it to optimize based on that. Profit.

comments.author: biggdogg420
comments.body: On my Godot browser remake of Birth of the Federation, average FPS hid the problem: a player felt the title menu hitch even after preload and refresh. I used Claude Code to help trace frame times. In the current WebGL build we wait for a short pause in input before starting some shader prep. The same tester found WebGL smoother than the WebGPU path their browser picked, but still reported some menu and UI hitches. If you’ve already gained 12–15 FPS, I’d capture a frame-time trace while repeating one action that still feels bad. Do you see a few long frames on that action, or is the whole scene consistently slow? That will give Claude something concrete to work on.

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
Well you will get some results if you literally just tell Claude to 'optimize this game pls make it run better' but you're going to hit a wall soon and miss a ton of optimizations.

What you really want to do is something like set up a performance recorder with deep profiling of functions enabled and choose multiple segments of this game of varying levels and intensities and scenes. Then record a multiple minute profiler for each of these scenes while actually simulating a player playing that segment. Then I want you to go through each recording and identify largest garbage collection allocations and stutter, functions that take huge portions of frame time, general lag spikes, general low FPS and generally identify everything that is taking the largest portion of frame time. List all of these and sort by the worst impact. Then for each item web search the optimal way to improve performance in this current game engine and let's start optimizing the ones you consider safe starting with the worst culprits first. Create multiple tests first for each segment. Then optimize and ensure all tests still pass after optimization. 

Record down in claude.md or related docs/memories the problems identified to ensure we do not re-introduce the same issues in the future. Also create deterministic guard scripts and tests that will validate this in our CI build and automated tests.
